title: Smart Agri UGM Lecturers and Researchers Visit Kyushu University, Japan, to Strengthen Smart Farming Research Collaboration
excerpt: Meeting with Prof. Takashi Okayasu, Ph.D. Yogyakarta, December 7, 2024 – Ir. Andri Prima Nugroho, STP., M.Sc., Ph.D., IPU., ASEAN Eng., research coordinator of the Smart Agriculture Research Center (SARC) and lecturer at the Department of Agricultural Engineering and Biosystems, Faculty of Agricultural Technology, Universitas Gadjah Mada (UGM), has just completed…
body:
Meeting with Prof. Takashi Okayasu, Ph.D.

Yogyakarta, December 7, 2024 – Ir. Andri Prima Nugroho, STP., M.Sc., Ph.D., IPU., ASEAN Eng., research coordinator of the Smart Agriculture Research Center (SARC) and lecturer at the Department of Agricultural Engineering and Biosystems, Faculty of Agricultural Technology, Universitas Gadjah Mada (UGM), has just completed a research visit to Kyushu University, Japan, from late November to early December 2024. This visit was part of a joint supervision and research program funded by the Directorate of Partnership and Global Relations at UGM.

During his visit, Dr. Andri conducted a series of activities, including meetings with Prof. Takashi Okayasu and his research team at the Agricultural Machinery and Production System Design Laboratory (Lab. AMPSD), as well as Prof. Takahiro Fujiwara at the Forest Policy Laboratory, Kyushu University. The discussions focused on finalizing the Memorandum of Agreement (MoA) for the 2024 joint supervision program and exploring opportunities for further research collaboration, including a student exchange program.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/249-1-whatsapp-image-lab-meeting--1024x765.webp)

Dr. Andri attending a seminar meeting at the AMPSD Laboratory

Dr. Andri also had the opportunity to visit agricultural research facilities at Kyushu University, such as the smart greenhouse, and to discuss with students and researchers at Lab. AMPSD. He presented his research on smart agricultural technology in tropical regions, particularly the use of data to optimize agricultural productivity.

The visit resulted in an agreement to strengthen research collaboration between UGM and Kyushu University, especially in the fields of plant phenotyping and indoor agriculture. This collaboration is expected to produce joint publications in reputable international journals and enhance research capacity at both institutions. The success of this visit demonstrates UGM's commitment to expanding its international network and promoting innovation in agriculture.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/249-2-visiting-kyushu-japan-fasilitas-lab-1-1024x990.webp)

Facilities at the AMPSD Laboratory – Plant Phenotyping Technology

This collaboration is particularly timely given the mounting challenges to agricultural productivity caused by climate change. By leveraging advanced technology and research methodology, both institutions aim to develop sustainable agricultural practices that can withstand the impacts of climate change. This partnership aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly those focused on ending hunger, achieving food security, and promoting sustainable agriculture.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/249-3-visiting-kyushu-japan-meeting-with-dr.-fujiwara.webp)

Meeting with Dr. Takahiro Fujiwara (Forest Policy)

Beyond academic discussions, Dr. Andri emphasized the importance of integrating local knowledge with modern agricultural practices. He believes that understanding the unique challenges faced by farmers in tropical regions is essential for developing effective solutions that increase agricultural productivity while remaining environmentally friendly.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/249-4-visitng-kyushu-2024-11-27-iop-consortium-1024x768.webp)

An opportunity to meet with the Internet of Plant Consortium with guests from Wageningen University and Research Netherlands, Dr. Joseph Peller

The visit also provided an opportunity for cultural exchange, as Dr. Andri and his team learned about Japanese agricultural practices and innovations. This exchange of knowledge is vital for building a collaborative spirit and understanding between the two institutions, which can lead to more effective research outcomes.

As UGM continues to strengthen its global partnerships, this visit to Kyushu University marks a significant step toward achieving its goals in agricultural research and innovation. This collaboration is expected to benefit not only the institutions involved but also contribute to the broader goal of developing sustainable agriculture in the face of climate change.

original.body:
Meeting dengan Prof. Takashi Okayasu, Ph.D.

Yogyakarta, 7 Desember 2024 – Ir. Andri Prima Nugroho, STP., M.Sc., Ph.D., IPU., ASEAN Eng., koordinator riset Smart Agriculture Research Center (SARC) dan dosen Departemen Teknik Pertanian dan Biosistem, Fakultas Teknologi Pertanian, Universitas Gadjah Mada (UGM), baru saja menyelesaikan kunjungan riset ke Kyushu University, Jepang, dari akhir November hingga awal Desember 2024. Kunjungan ini merupakan bagian dari program _joint supervision and research_ yang didanai oleh Direktorat Kemitraan dan Relasi Global UGM.

Selama kunjungannya, Dr. Andri melakukan serangkaian kegiatan, termasuk pertemuan dengan Prof. Takashi Okayasu dan tim risetnya di Laboratorium Agricultural Machinery and Production System Design (Lab. AMPSD), serta Prof. Takahiro Fujiwara di Laboratorium Forest Policy, Kyushu University. Diskusi difokuskan pada finalisasi Memorandum of Agreement (MoA) untuk program joint supervision tahun 2024 dan menjajaki peluang kerjasama riset lebih lanjut, termasuk program pertukaran mahasiswa.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/249-1-whatsapp-image-lab-meeting--1024x765.webp)

Dr. Andri mengikuti meeting Seminar di Laboratorium AMPSD

Dr. Andri juga berkesempatan untuk mengunjungi fasilitas riset pertanian di Kyushu University, seperti _smart greenhouse_, dan berdiskusi dengan mahasiswa dan peneliti di Lab. AMPSD. Ia mempresentasikan risetnya tentang teknologi pertanian cerdas di daerah tropis, khususnya pemanfaatan data untuk optimasi produktivitas pertanian.

Kunjungan ini menghasilkan kesepakatan untuk memperkuat kerjasama riset antara UGM dan Kyushu University, khususnya di bidang plant phenotyping dan pertanian indoor. Kerjasama ini diharapkan dapat menghasilkan publikasi bersama di jurnal internasional bereputasi dan meningkatkan kapasitas riset di kedua institusi. Keberhasilan kunjungan ini menunjukkan komitmen UGM dalam memperluas jejaring internasional dan mendorong inovasi di bidang pertanian.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/249-2-visiting-kyushu-japan-fasilitas-lab-1-1024x990.webp)

Fasilitas di Laboratorium AMPSD – Plant Phenotyping Technology

Kerjasama ini sangat tepat waktu mengingat tantangan yang semakin meningkat akibat perubahan iklim terhadap produktivitas pertanian. Dengan memanfaatkan teknologi canggih dan metodologi riset, kedua institusi bertujuan untuk mengembangkan praktik pertanian berkelanjutan yang dapat bertahan dari dampak perubahan iklim. Kemitraan ini sejalan dengan Tujuan Pembangunan Berkelanjutan (SDGs), khususnya yang berfokus pada mengakhiri kelaparan, mencapai ketahanan pangan, dan mempromosikan pertanian berkelanjutan.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/249-3-visiting-kyushu-japan-meeting-with-dr.-fujiwara.webp)

Meeting dengan Dr. Takahiro Fujiwara (Forest Policy)

Selain diskusi akademis, Dr. Andri menekankan pentingnya mengintegrasikan pengetahuan lokal dengan praktik pertanian modern. Ia percaya bahwa memahami tantangan unik yang dihadapi petani di daerah tropis sangat penting untuk mengembangkan solusi efektif yang meningkatkan produktivitas pertanian sambil tetap ramah lingkungan.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/249-4-visitng-kyushu-2024-11-27-iop-consortium-1024x768.webp)

Kesempatan meeting dengan Internet of Plant Consortium dengan tamu dari Wageningen University and Research Netherlands, Dr. Joseph Peller

Kunjungan ini juga memberikan kesempatan untuk pertukaran budaya, karena Dr. Andri dan timnya belajar tentang praktik dan inovasi pertanian Jepang. Pertukaran pengetahuan ini sangat penting untuk membangun semangat kolaboratif dan pemahaman antara kedua institusi, yang dapat mengarah pada hasil riset yang lebih efektif.

Seiring UGM terus memperkuat kemitraan globalnya, kunjungan ke Kyushu University ini menandai langkah signifikan menuju pencapaian tujuan dalam riset dan inovasi pertanian. Kerjasama ini diharapkan tidak hanya memberikan manfaat bagi institusi yang terlibat tetapi juga berkontribusi pada tujuan yang lebih luas dalam pengembangan pertanian berkelanjutan di tengah perubahan iklim.
